title: Counterfeit Ledger Nano S Plus opened by Cos (@evilcos)

purchase.dateNote: Cos said he bought it from JD.com in mainland China, without giving the seller's name or the order date.

components: One QFN chip printed with the Ledger logo and no part number, in place of the ST33 secure element (U4) and STM32F042K6 MCU (U2)
40 MHz crystal (X1, marked 40.000), which suggests an Espressif ESP32-family chip; the genuine STM32F042 needs no crystal
Buttons on the lower edge, labelled S2, where the genuine board has SW1 and SW2 on the upper edge
No board-maker markings, where the genuine board has E232940, JVE-M2 and a JOVE3 2203 date code
implant.notes: Cos (@evilcos) opened a Nano S Plus and posted its board next to the board in Ledger's official support article, asking where the backdoor part was. Yishi (@ohyishi) replied that it is a counterfeit: the whole board is different, and it has no secure element. The one main chip carries a Ledger logo instead of a maker's name and part number, and the 40 MHz crystal points to an ESP32. Yishi also linked it to fake Nano S Plus units reported in spring 2026. A Brazilian researcher bought one of those on a Chinese e-commerce site. Its chip markings were ground off, and its firmware called itself "Nano S+ V2.1". It stored the PIN and recovery phrase in plain text and sent them to the attackers' server. A QR code in the box led to a fake Ledger Live that showed a fake genuineness check. Cos agreed this device is from that wave, and said it still worked when tested. Mark Karpelès (@MagicalTux) replied that the board has no remote communication like the spy implants. He said it would likely show as not genuine in Ledger Wallet, and might give a predetermined seed. This is the same board as @zhongbentong7's second device. Cos later confirmed that he bought it from JD.com (京东) in mainland China. He didn't say whether it was JD's own store or a third-party seller on the platform.

我刚刚拆了一个 Ledger Nano S Plus（图上），和官方 PCB 正面（图下）居然如此不同…那么后门元件在哪？…或者我遗漏了什么？@Ledger 😵‍💫

https://support.ledger.com/zh-CN/article/4404382029329-zd

(Chinese: "I just took apart a Ledger Nano S Plus (top picture), and it's surprisingly different from the front of the official PCB (bottom picture)… So where is the backdoor part? …Or did I miss something?")

sources.author: Yishi
sources.text:
这个很像假货。…

(Chinese, summarised: "This looks like a fake." It has no secure element: a genuine Nano S Plus has two ST chips, the STM32F042K6 (U2) and the ST33 (U4). The main chip has only a Ledger logo and no part number. The extra 40 MHz crystal (X1, marked 40.000) points to an Espressif ESP32. The layout and silkscreen are different: the genuine board has SW1 and SW2 on the upper edge and the board-maker marks E232940 and JOVE3 2203.)

sources.author: Yishi
sources.text:
今年春天有人公开过同一类假 Nano S Plus。…

(Chinese, summarised: The same kind of fake Nano S Plus was made public this spring. A Brazilian security researcher bought one on a Chinese e-commerce site. Its chip markings were ground off, and the firmware reported itself as "Nano S+ V2.1", with Espressif shown as the maker. It replaces the secure element with an ESP32, stores the PIN and recovery phrase in plain text, and sends them to the attackers' server. A QR code in the box leads to a fake Ledger Live with a fake genuineness check. This one has a printed Ledger logo instead of ground-off markings, so it may be a newer version from the same group, or another copy.)

sources.author: Mark Karpelès
sources.text: @evilcos @Ledger This is not a valid board for the Ledger S plus, but it doesn't have the remote communication capabilities of the spy implants. This is likely going to show as "not genuine" in ledger wallet, and will give you a predetermined seed or something like that.

images.caption: Top: the counterfeit board, with one Ledger-logo chip, the 40 MHz crystal (X1) and buttons on the lower edge. Bottom: the genuine board from Ledger's support article, with the STM32F042K6 (U2), the ST33 secure element (U4), and buttons SW1 and SW2 on the upper edge.
